title: The Impact of Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Artificial Intelligence on Students’ Motivation and Achievement in STEM Education: A Systematic Review
venue: Journal of Educational Studies in Mathematics and Computer Science
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how intelligent tutoring systems (ITS) with integrated artificial intelligence affect students’ motivation and academic achievement in STEM education. The central research question asks how ITSs supported by AI influence student motivation and achievement, with particular attention to STEM subjects such as mathematics, science, and computer science.

The intervention studied is not a single program but the broader use of AI-enabled intelligent tutoring systems in STEM education. The authors conducted a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines and identified 24 studies published between 2020 and May 2024 from Science Direct, Springer Open, and Google Scholar. Across the reviewed studies, ITS interventions commonly involved personalized feedback, adaptive learning pathways, visualization, simulation, and interactive support designed to mimic or supplement human tutoring.

The reviewed evidence primarily concerns students, especially those in K–12 settings, although some higher education studies were also included. The review reports that the majority of included research focused on mathematics, computer science, and science learning. The context varies across studies, including technology-supported and sometimes blended learning environments, but the review emphasizes formal STEM education settings rather than a single site or country.

The main conclusion is that ITS and AI generally have a positive effect on student motivation and academic achievement in STEM education. Of the 24 included studies, 20 were reported as showing positive effects and 4 negative or null effects. The review concludes that personalized and adaptive features are especially important in improving engagement and performance, while also noting that the evidence base remains limited and that more long-term, diverse, and methodologically rigorous research is needed.

identified_tools.name: Intelligent Tutoring Systems with AI
identified_tools.description: AI-enabled tutoring systems that provide instructional support, guidance, feedback, and adaptive learning pathways to learners.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of studies on ITS and AI-supported tutoring in STEM education, mainly comparing ITS/AI-supported learning with traditional or non-ITS instruction in K–12 and some higher education contexts.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that 15 studies (62.5%) found increased student motivation associated with ITS/AI-supported learning in STEM education.
The review reports that 17 studies (70.83%) found improvement in academic performance associated with ITS/AI-supported learning.

For student achievement, the review reports 14 studies with positive effects, 3 studies with no significant difference, and 2 studies with negative effects relative to comparison conditions, indicating mostly positive but not uniform evidence.
Within mathematics-focused studies, the review reports 10 studies with positive findings and 2 with negative findings for motivation and/or achievement outcomes under ITS/AI-supported learning.
Within computer science-focused studies, the review reports 7 studies with positive findings and 1 with negative findings for motivation and/or achievement outcomes under ITS/AI-supported learning.
Within science-focused studies, the review reports 4 studies with positive findings and no negative findings for motivation and/or achievement outcomes under ITS/AI-supported learning.

identified_tools.name: PhET
identified_tools.description: An interactive physics and STEM simulation platform used for teaching and learning through visual, manipulable simulations.
identified_tools.use_case: The review specifically mentions 'PhET simulations' in the summary of Susilawati et al. (2022), stating that PhET simulations and ITS systems boost motivation and problem-solving in physics and create a more engaging learning experience. It is discussed as a named educational technology used in STEM/physics instruction alongside ITS, not as a focal ITS product itself.

findings.finding_summary: PhET simulations were reported to improve physics problem-solving in the reviewed discussion of Susilawati et al. (2022).
PhET simulations were reported to increase student motivation and create a more engaging learning experience in physics.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic review conducted with PRISMA procedures, which places it above single observational studies. However, it is not a formal meta-analysis with pooled effect sizes and includes heterogeneous studies with acknowledged selection and reporting limitations, so green is more appropriate than blue.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports mostly positive effects on motivation and achievement, but it does not provide a pooled effect size and notes some null or negative findings. Because the magnitude of impact is unclear and based on heterogeneous included studies, the impact is best classified as yellow.
